newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia, France to produce rolling stock wheels.
newsitem.headline: Serbia, France to produce rolling stock wheels.

text.p: Serbia's rail company and French firm Valdunes have signed an 80-million French franc deal for joint production of rolling stock wheels and axles, the Serbian transport ministry said on Thursday.

The five-year deal was signed by Zeleznicko Transportno Preduzece (ZTP) Beograd General Manager Zivorad Maksimovic and Valdunes General Manager Jean-Pierre Auger on Wednesday, the ministry said in a press release faxed to Reuters.

"The agreement on industrial cooperation, joint investment and commercial production of rolling stock wheels is a continuation of the good cooperation between Serbia's railroad and the French partner before the trade embargo was imposed on Yugoslavia," Transport Minister Svetolik Kostadinovic said.

ZTP Beograd and Valdunes, a member of the French ferrous metallurgy concern Usinor Sacilor, signed a letter of intent in October 1996, after war-related international sanctions against Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, were lifted.
Under the deal, rolling stock wheels wrought by Valdunes will be machine processed by Zelvoz of Smederevo, a subsidiary of ZTP Beograd.

Valdunes will invest modern equipment, transfer technology and provide technical assistance and training to Zelvoz and ZTP Beograd, while ZTP Beograd will invest production and business premises with existing equipment and infrastruture.
Valdunes has already sent the first 500 rail car wheels for processing in Zelvoz, while 100 axle blocks for high speed wagons, produced by Gosa of Smederevska Palanka, will be delivered in June.
The new production line for processing rolling stock wheels, not produced in Yugoslavia before, is expected to be put into operation in the fall, the ministry said.

The Yugoslav-French joint venture firm, with an annual capacity of 12,000 rolling stock wheels, will satisfy the needs of rail companies in Yugoslavia as well as in its neighbourhood, the ministry said.

It will also meet the needs of large industrial systems such as Sartid steel works, Elektroprivreda Srbije power company, Rudarsko topionicarski basen Bor copper mining and smelting complex, Naftna industrija Srbije oil company and others that have their own rail capacities.

The deal will translate into greater capacity utilisation for local rolling stock manufacturers and overhaulers such as Gosa, Fabrika Vagona Kraljevo, Masinska industrija Nis, Bratstvo of Subotica and Sinvoz of Zrenjaninin.
The joint enterprise will later expand its activities to include processing of axles and axle blocks.
